title: Trap! Trap! Trap!
summary: Attack the rook with the king while the knight forks every safe retreat.

nodes.question: Can Re3 escape the approaching king without a fork?
nodes.explanation: Begin after ...Kxb7: White has Kg1/Nd7/b2/g2 against Kb7/Re3/e7. The earlier eight-piece pawn offer and Nd7 setup remain source context outside this checked tree.

branches.title: Fork after ...Rd3
commentary: Begin after ...Kxb7 in the seven-piece source diagram. The king attack exposes the rook’s limited safe retreats.
Kf2 attacks Re3. Nd7 and the king cover most of the rook’s escape squares.
Rd3 is one of the illustrated safe rook retreats, but it lands on a knight-fork square.
Nc5+ checks Kb7 and attacks the rook on d3. The rook cannot escape before Black answers the check.
Kc6 is a representative legal king completion supplied independently beyond the illustrated fork.
Nxd3 collects the rook. The exact knight-and-pawn ending is winning; further conversion is not presented as immediate mate.
branches.classification: independent alternative with representative legal replies

exercises.prompt: Why does the king attack work despite the rook’s long range?
exercises.answer: Kf2 and Nd7 cover its immediate escapes. The safe d3/e4/e6/b3 retreats each allow Nc5+, forking the rook and Kb7.
